title: White does not play c4 and e4
intro:
# White does not play c4 and e4: the London, the Colle, the Trompowsky and the Torre

Most club players with the White pieces do not play the main lines. They play a system: the bishop to f4 and a pawn triangle, the bishop to g5 before anything else, or the quiet e3 and Bd3. The four Black moves do not change, and the plans mostly do not either: ...d6, ...Nbd7 and ...e5, with the rook on e8 behind the pawn. What changes is the moment, because a bishop on f4 or g5 is looking at the square the lever needs.

## The London: 2.Bf4

The London player's own course, this app's first, says what White does against this setup: the bishop to e2 rather than d3, h3 before the lever comes so that the bishop has h2, and c4 rather than c3 because Black declined to put a pawn on d5. This chapter's Black moves are answers to that. The lever is prepared with ...Nbd7 and ...Re8, and when it comes after c4 the trade on e5 is met with the pawn, and the knight goes to e4 or to h5 depending on what White has done with the bishop. If White plays c3 instead, the lever waits: ...b6 and ...Bb7 first, because after c3 the trade on e5 and a knight landing there is a pawn.

## The Trompowsky and the Torre: a bishop on g5

The bishop on g5 before ...g6 has been answered, and 2...g6 is still the move: if the bishop takes on f6 the e-pawn takes back and Black has the bishop pair for a doubled pawn that holds e5 and g5 both. The Torre, with the knight on f3 first, is quieter: the same ...d6, ...Nbd7 and ...e5, then ...h6 to ask the bishop and ...Qe8 or ...Re8 to break the pin.

## The Colle: e3 and Bd3

The quietest of all, and the one where the lever comes with the most behind it: ...Nbd7, ...e5, and when White plays e4 the position is the Classical's open centre with White's bishop on d3 in the way of the queen. If White adds c4 it is chapter 3's plans with a bishop on d3 rather than g2.

## Typical mistakes at this level

Playing ...e5 against the London with nothing behind it, so that dxe5 and a knight on e5 win a pawn. Meeting Bg5 with ...Ne4 and a pawn grab that a club player has prepared. Taking on d4 in the Colle before the knight on d7 is ready to go to c5. And forgetting, against the systems, that the plan is the same as against the main lines: the lever, the rook to e8, the knight to c5 or e4.
